title: Webflow Template Marketplace Impact Reports
headline: A PM-ready report packet now connects Marketplace Code Components, richer search, Validator app enforcement, Asset Dashboard routing, and agent-review guardrails to the current business trajectory.

artifactUrls.label: Report packet in repo
artifactUrls.summary: Public-reviewable Markdown packet for PMs and business stakeholders.

summary: The report collection frames the current Marketplace work as a coordinated quality and conversion program: richer discovery through Code Components and webflow-search, stronger creator preflight through the Validator app, clearer creator recovery through the Asset Dashboard, and tighter reviewer/agent guardrails.

The business read is intentionally balanced. Early data shows stabilization and stronger downstream CTA/order behavior, but not yet a recovery in the browse-to-template selection step that drove the multi-month decline.

The packet separates repo-backed implementation evidence from live analytics notes. PMs can use the repo links for public review while treating Amplitude, Clarity, and Datadog numbers as refresh-required operational evidence.
Two blockers remain important for interpretation: unresolved desktop Safari/WebKit script errors and missing normalized analytics properties for signal-level attribution.
The next strategic bet is an agentic Webflow MCP experiment that measures an agent-native discovery path as its own cohort rather than hiding it inside bot-diluted web traffic.

clientUpdate: The Webflow Template Marketplace report packet is ready for PM/business review. It gives a public-reviewable repo trail for the implementation work and a balanced impact read for what has changed.

The strongest read is that the work is directionally correct and appears to have stabilized downstream conversion, but it has not yet proven a recovery in browse-to-template selection. That remains the main metric to watch.

Validator app enforcement and Asset Dashboard routing should improve creator preparedness and reduce reviewer ambiguity. Review-agent output remains supplemental evidence rather than a replacement for human reviewer decisions.
Measurement still needs engineering follow-up before signal-level conclusions are reliable: Safari/WebKit errors remain a risk, and normalized attribution properties are not yet landing in Amplitude.
The agentic Webflow MCP experiment should be framed as a new agent-native discovery cohort, not as a replacement for human Marketplace browsing.
nextReview: Refresh Amplitude, Clarity, and Datadog before presenting final impact claims.
Resolve or explicitly rule out the desktop Safari/WebKit script-error issue.
Fix normalized analytics property delivery for signal_window, signal_density, attribution_present, and attribution_match.
Use browse-to-template selection as the Marketplace top-of-funnel success metric.
Scope the Webflow MCP experiment with separate agent attribution and guardrails.
